claims: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends visiting a travel medicine specialist or your healthcare provider 4–6 weeks before departure to discuss your itinerary and receive tailored advice.
The CDC has issued a Level 2 travel advisory for over 30 countries due to polio detections.
Specific countries in Africa and South America require proof of yellow fever vaccination (Yellow Card).
The Yellow Card is only valid 10 days after administration.
Yellow fever vaccination is required for entry into certain countries in Africa and South America.
Hepatitis A vaccination is recommended for most travelers going to countries with poor food/water sanitation.
Typhoid vaccination is recommended for travelers visiting South Asia (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh) or other areas with high risk.
Japanese Encephalitis vaccination is recommended for long-term travel (≥1 month) or rural visits in Asia.
Meningococcal Disease vaccination is recommended for the African meningitis belt.
Meningococcal Disease vaccination is required for Hajj/Umrah travelers to Saudi Arabia.
Rabies vaccination is recommended for travelers visiting areas where dog bites are common or for long-stay or rural travelers.
Tick-borne Encephalitis (TBE) vaccination is recommended for travelers going to TBE-endemic areas in Europe or Asia who plan outdoor activities.
The minimum time needed for yellow fever vaccine to become effective for entry requirements is 10 days.
Hepatitis A vaccine can still offer protection if given less than 2 weeks before travel.
CVS MinuteClinic offers consultations and vaccinations.
